steps.content: Désir stands aloof in WhiteSands, a solitary oasis, ringed by endless dunes. This spot behind the inn is the only place with an unobstructed view. From here, one can gaze upon DisCity in the distance—an unknown yet promising land beyond the sands.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Making progress, little Chief. You didn't get lost this time.

Gazing into WhiteSands, Vautour Bleu turns at your footsteps. Her gaze catch yours, and for a moment, it's as if you're both back on the balconies, about to pick up the thread of your usual chat through the windows.
But now, the peaceful disguise has all been torn away, shattered both in dreams and reality.
So this is what you said the most picturesque spot?
All you see is but the deceptively calm expanse of WhiteSands, with DisCity barely visible on the far horizon. But sightseeing is the last thing on your mind right now.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: I'm sure you've seen far more impressive sights in DisCity. To you, such a barren desert is probably nothing remarkable. But to the people of Désir, it's precious.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: This is the only spot in town where you can see DisCity—though not always clearly. When sandstorms sweep across or the weather turns, all you can make out is a hazy outline.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Distance makes it special. Everyone can paint their own picture of DisCity, filling it in with the most magnificent scenery. But I suspect those who actually live here don't really look at it that way.
With a hint of wistfulness, Vautour Bleu drifts back with a gentle question.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: During your stay, have you had a chance to eat at Alba's diner yet?
Not just Alba's diner, I've tried Liam's delivered milk also, and Primrose's bread.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: They're all good kids. It's because of them that people in Désir can still enjoy fleeting moments of happiness.
But is that real happiness? You keep the question to yourself.
I've passed by it, but haven't eaten there yet.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Ah, that's a shame. You really should give it a try. Alba's a good girl, and she's done wonders with that place.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: The red wine they serve is exceptional too. It can hold its own against some of the finest vintages from DisCity.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: It took Alba ages to master how to brew. Poor Juan was roped into being her taster. I hear he nearly swore off drinking altogether by the end. The recipe itself is actually a legacy from when Désir was a holiday resort.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Did you know? This place used to be popular. The wealthy from DisCity would flock to this oasis for their getaways.
The Outland Affairs Bureau briefed me on it.
There's no point in hiding anything now that she's blown your cover.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: I knew who they'd send, but they've prepped you more thoroughly than I anticipated. Enlighten me, what else did they tell you?

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Ah no, let me guess. They probably painted us as a bunch of squatters or some band of lowlifes, wasting our days chasing pipe dreams. Am I close?
Your mind flashes back to Guillotin's briefing. The Outland Affairs Bureau's attitude is indeed just as Vautour Bleu describes.
You seem to know DisCity better than I expected.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: And how much do you know about Désir now?
It's an elaborate trap you perpetuate with lies. You lure in those desperate for a taste of DisCity life, let them chase a dream they'll never catch.
Thinking of Sheila and those despairing specters, you can't keep your tone friendly.
Still, Vautour Bleu remains unperturbed, drifting her gaze toward WhiteSands.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: I don't believe I've told you how I brought them to Désir, have I?

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: I still remember the first time I met Sheila. Our caravan was just passing through Velvet Valley. When her parents heard I could take people to DisCity, they entrusted her to me without a second thought.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: When we departed, her parents saw her off at the door. "You'll get better once you're in DisCity! They'll cure you there!" They kept calling out, and Sheila left with a smile on her face.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: But I could see her condition. Her M-value was already close to the mutation threshold. It was Mania that caused her illness, brought on by the disasters.
Mania?

steps.speaker: Sheila
steps.content: What it is like in DisCity... Will the medicine be expensive there? Will the doctors there be impatient with me too...?

steps.speaker: Sheila
steps.content: Will they... shun me for my sickness, like everyone back home...?
Even DisCity hasn't found a cure for Mania yet.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: But the people beyond DisCity's walls don't know that. To them, it's almost a holy ground. They've pinned all their hopes for the future on this mirage.
You knew it from the start that Sheila's wish would never come true, then why did you...?
"Why did you still take Sheila in?" Your question dies on your lips. It was not Vautour Bleu, but her Mania-fearing hometown and her own family who had sent her away.
Vautour Bleu casts a knowing gaze at you, and continues her story.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: And Primrose, we found her lying in the snow, without even a rough shelter. The poor girl didn't have a sliver of identity proof. Turns out her aunt and uncle had already told everyone she'd died of illness. When she heard we were headed to DisCity, she was almost begging us...
Vautour Bleu bends down, scooping up a handful of sand, then watches it slip through her fingers.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: WhiteSands is vast, but fertile soil for hope is rare. Rarer still are unyielding rocks that can weather the storms. Most of what you see is just this—fine sand, carried here by winds, blowing toward DisCity.

The truths, blowing in the wind, weigh heavy: Sheila's sickness, incurable; Liam's mother, not waiting in DisCity; Alba, never to be a beauty queen... Vautour Bleu has the means to bring them to DisCity, yet she chooses not to strip away the last threads of hope these fragile souls cling to.
Was Sheila really killed by the monsters?
She already knew about the flowers, even seized the chance to write that letter. She could've hidden somewhere safe with datura. So what really killed her? The monsters—or Mania and her own despair?
A weary smile flickers across Vautour Bleu's face. You've edged close to the truth she's guarding, yet neither of you has the heart to say it out.
Sheila wasn't the only one with an M-value nearing the threshold, was she?
The moment these people started their impossible dreams of DisCity, they were already teetering on the edge of mutation.
Vautour Bleu stoops down, her fingers gently brushing away the sand. In the pit lie buried countless withered datura leaves.
[Town center]
Meanwhile, throughout the town, datura flowers begin to wither, their fragrance gradually dissipating.
Freed from the numbing scents, the monsters start appearing, growing restless among the townsfolk.

steps.speaker: Townie B
steps.content: What... what's that sound?

steps.speaker: Townie A
steps.content: I hear it too... It's getting closer.
Eerie noises echo throughout the town. They seem to be coming from just beyond the datura-covered fences.

steps.speaker: Townie B
steps.content: What's happened to these flowers? They've all died.

A townsman approaches the fence, reaching out to pluck off the withered datura flowers. He peeks out curiously through a gap in the planks, and when his gaze reaches something beyond, the color drains from his face.

steps.speaker: Townie B
steps.content: Ahhh! Monsters! There are monsters in the town!!!
